paras: Ask an operations director to describe a normal day and you will get an uncomfortable silence. There is no normal day. Monday is usually the exception: the senior team meets at headquarters, the numbers from the previous week are on the table, and the deadline for the monthly report is never far away. From Tuesday the shape breaks. One week you spend three days on site, in a warehouse where the night shift starts at ten. The next week you barely leave your desk.

This is why two tenses live side by side in that job. "I run four areas" is always true. "This month I am running a project with a new supplier" is true only for now. People who confuse the two sound strange in both directions: they say they are living in Sao Paulo for twenty years, or that they visit a warehouse today. The rule is quiet but firm. If it is your life, use the simple form. If it is your week, use the -ing. And when the workload doubles, say so in the continuous, because it will not last forever.

reading.prompt: What is the best title for this text?
choices: Why operations directors work too many hours
Two tenses for a job with no normal day
How to plan a perfect weekly schedule

items: Monday usually has a fixed shape in this job.
t
The text says Monday is usually the exception: the senior team meets at headquarters.
The text says you should use the -ing form for things that are always true.
f
It says the opposite: if it is your life, use the simple form; if it is your week, use the -ing.
The night shift in the warehouse starts at ten.
t
The text says a warehouse where the night shift starts at ten.
Scenario 1
A colleague abroad asks what your job is and what you are doing this month. Answer both parts, and make the tenses different.
Scenario 2
Somebody asks why you are not at your desk this week. Explain where you are and why, and say what you normally do instead.
Scenario 3
Your workload has doubled because of one project. Describe the situation to your manager without sounding like it is permanent.

items.situation: It is Tuesday morning and you are in a warehouse instead of the office. A supplier calls and asks where you are. Answer in two sentences.
tips: Where you are now goes in the continuous: "I am visiting..."
Then add the routine: "I usually spend Tuesdays..."

items.situation: A colleague asks how many people work the night shift and how it is going this week.
tips: The number is a fact: simple form.
How it is going this week: continuous.

items.situation: Your manager asks whether the workload is always this heavy, or only now.
tips: Say which part is permanent and which part is temporary.

items.situation: Somebody asks what you are working on right now, and you want to give more than three words.
tips: Name the project, the stage, and the deadline.
Finish with what happens next week.

items.situation: A new manager asks you to explain the difference between headquarters and on site, in your own words.
tips: Define each one in one sentence.
Then say how often you are in each place.

answerkey.title: Reveal the model answers
list: This week I am visiting the warehouse.
We always work with that supplier.
The night shift is starting later than usual tonight.
I deal with three deadlines every month.
answerkey.note: The time word decides the tense, not the verb. Change the time word and the tense has to follow.

listenings.text: Felipe, it is Megan with your week. The results meeting is still Monday at nine, at headquarters, and the report deadline has not moved. Tuesday is the problem. The audit team is arriving in the morning, so you are not going to the store after all. On Wednesday you are traveling to the warehouse, and you are staying there until Thursday afternoon, because the night shift wants twenty minutes with you. Friday is open for now. I am following up on the supplier contract today and I will send you the file tonight.

Morning, Felipe. Ian here, from the warehouse. Quick update before you arrive. We normally receive four trucks a day, but this week we are receiving seven, because two suppliers moved their dates. The night shift is dealing with the extra volume and nobody is complaining yet, although the workload is heavy. One machine is not working properly, so maintenance is coming on Thursday. Everything else is running as usual. See you on site on Wednesday.

extra_audio.text: First, Megan confirms that the results meeting is still on Monday at headquarters. Then she explains that the audit team is arriving on Tuesday morning. After that, she says the store visit is cancelled. Next, she describes the two days at the warehouse. Finally, she promises to follow up on the supplier contract.
